lemonde.fr/en.title: Israeli settlers beat AFP photographer in occupied West Bank
lemonde.fr/en.text:
Armed Israeli settlers on Tuesday, October 6, beat an Agence France-Presse (AFP) photographer, leaving him requiring hospital treatment, as he covered ongoing violence by settlers against West Bank olive farmers. Jaafar Ashtiyeh, 58, a veteran photographer for the international news agency in the Palestinian territory, had tried to rush into a car for safety but two men tackled him down and clobbered him with their rifle butts, according to witnesses, his family and fellow journalists.
Ashtiyeh and another AFP photographer, John Wessels, were standing on a hill near the northern village of Aqraba watching the olive harvest from around 500 meters away when they saw an Israeli soldier detain a Palestinian. As Ashtiyeh took pictures, a man suddenly opened live fire as he raced in a quad bike up a hill towards the journalists.
One Palestinian dropped to the ground. He was also hospitalized, with a gunshot to the foot, according to the Palestine Red Crescent Society. At least six other people then ran towards the AFP journalists firing guns, with two of them beating Ashtiyeh as he tried to enter the car, which was clearly marked "Press." "I could hear his screams," said Wessels, who was also threatened at gunpoint.
Ashtiyeh, who is Palestinian, was rushed by ambulance to a hospital in Nablus. He underwent X-rays which did not detect broken bones but he will remain in hospital for round-the-clock observation, said his son, Zain Jaafar. The assailants stole Ashtiyeh's camera equipment, Wessels said.
The violence took place despite the presence of at least a dozen fully equipped Israeli soldiers around 500 meters away, according to Wessels. The man who first fired the gun was wearing a long white shirt as well as military fatigue trousers and boots, which are commonly worn by soldiers, Wessels said.
AFP has reached out to the Israeli military for comment.
'Deeply alarmed'
"We strongly condemn yet another serious attack on journalists trying to report on events in the West Bank and demand a full investigation. It is unacceptable that journalists can be beaten and robbed by armed settlers in front of Israeli security forces who made no attempt to intervene," said Phil Chetwynd, AFP's global news director.
The Foreign Press Association, which represents international media in Israel and the Palestinian territories, said it was "deeply alarmed." "Israeli authorities must investigate why soldiers present in the area did not intervene in this attack against clearly identified journalists," it said.
"This attack is a blatant attempt to intimidate the press and obstruct accurate reporting from the West Bank. International media have a responsibility to tell all sides of the story and will not be deterred by physical assaults or threats."
Reporters Without Borders said it condemned the attack "in the strongest terms." "Israeli settlers' attacks against journalists, carried out with complete impunity, are becoming more and more frequent in the West Bank," said the advocacy group known by its French initials RSF.
Israeli authorities have detained 19 journalists in the West Bank, including one AFP contributor, in the three years since the October 7, 2023 attack on Israel by Gaza-based Hamas, according to Paris-based Reporters Without Borders.
Ashtiyeh was attacked almost exactly a year earlier during the olive harvest by settlers who threw stones at him and who then set his car ablaze. In October, a settler hit another AFP journalist in the chin as he covered religious Jewish peace activists who seek to protect Palestinians from violence.
Violence has flared in recent months in the West Bank with near-daily attacks, thefts or vandalism by Israeli settlers against Palestinians. There have also been attacks against Israelis, with a Palestinian shooting dead a settler last month. Extremist Israeli settlers have been seizing olive groves owned by Palestinians, who see the trees as a cultural symbol.
Some 500,000 Israeli settlers live in the West Bank, which Israel captured in 1967, among three million Palestinians. Settlements in occupied territory are illegal under international law.

lemonde.fr/en.title: With a financial crisis looming, what promises can French presidential candidates make?
lemonde.fr/en.text:
The aim was not only to convince lawmakers, but also to reassure the state's creditors. The result was a double failure. When the government presented its 2027 draft budget on October 1, the opposition rejected the bill, and the markets responded with skepticism that such a budget could ever pass through the deeply divided Assemblée Nationale.
As a sign of how vulnerable France has become, the country's interest rates jumped once again the very next day, reaching nearly 5% – a record since 2002. The spread between French and German interest rates rose to over 1.5 percentage points, the widest in 15 years. In addition to the general rise in fuel prices and interest rates due to global instability, France also faces a rapid deterioration of its economic and budgetary situation: Public debt now exceeds 119% of GDP, growth has stalled, unemployment is rising again, and voters' concerns over the cost of living are mounting across all demographics.
While this atmosphere has been a source of anxiety for the government, it has also become treacherous for presidential election candidates. How should they campaign when most financial indicators are deteriorating? And how can they promise to deliver on their commitments when there is so little economic visibility and almost no financial room to maneuver?
They all agree on how serious the situation is. Right-wing and centrist candidates have even recently sounded the alarm on the budgetary situation. Bruno Retailleau, the candidate for the conservative Les Républicains (LR) party, said that "the mechanisms of a crisis are being set in motion." Gabriel Attal, from the centrist Renaissance party, said that "disaster is not far off." Marine Le Pen, of the far-right Rassemblement National (RN), said she was just as concerned by the situation, describing the state as "on the brink of a bond crisis." The Socialists also described France's "economic, social, and budgetary situation" as "serious" in a letter sent to Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu on Friday, October 2.

lemonde.fr/en.title: Messi scores in emotional Argentina farewell
lemonde.fr/en.text:
Lionel Messi brought the curtain down on his 21-year international career on Tuesday, October 6, bidding farewell to adoring Argentina fans in an emotional final appearance for the former world champions in Buenos Aires. In a perfectly scripted finale, the 39-year-old widely regarded as the greatest football player in history signed off with his 126th international goal in front of 85,000 supporters as Argentina cruised to a 3-0 victory over Benin. Messi, playing in his record-extending 208th international, also provided the assist for the opening goal scored by veteran Nicolas Otamendi, with Nico Paz also scoring.
But the match was a footnote to the occasion itself, which saw Messi savoring the adulation of the Monumental Stadium crowd one last time for an event which had been billed as "The Last Tango."
"It was a huge source of pride for me to defend this jersey for more than 20 years," Messi told fans in a post-match address. "Not coming anymore is going to be deeply painful. I swear I'd like to play for the rest of my life, because playing for the Argentina national team is the most beautiful thing that can happen to you."
Messi, though, said he had no regrets about his decision to retire, citing Argentina's grueling World Cup campaign, which took place as his late father was seriously ill, as a factor. "Even though I want to be here all my life, I feel that this is the moment. The last World Cup was too much, everything I had to live through," said Messi.
Beforehand, Messi wiped away tears as the bus carrying him and his Argentina teammates made its way through crowds of well-wishers en route to the stadium.
Messi took the field alongside his three children and received affectionate waves from his wife, Antonela Roccuzzo, and his mother, Celia Cuccittini, who were watching from a VIP box. Shortly before kick-off, a giant Argentina jersey bearing the word "Gracias" (Thank You) above the football superstar's No.10 was laid out on the pitch as the crowd roared their approval.
Messi welled up again as Falklands War veteran Fabio Santana sang the national anthem beside a banner which read – "The Malvinas are Argentine" – the same banner held aloft by players after their 2-1 World Cup semi-final win over England. The match was halted in the 10th minute – in tribute to Messi's famous shirt number – for a minute-long ovation to the former Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain star. He crowned the occasion with a goal from the penalty spot in the 71st minute.
'Gave it my all'
At the final whistle, a drone show lit up the night sky above the stadium, showing Messi's image and thanking the eight-time Ballon D'Or winner for his career. Messi's farewell came two and a half months after Argentina's World Cup final defeat to Spain in New Jersey, where Messi exited in tears after making little impression in an ill-tempered 1-0 loss. "I gave it my all; I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are great young players coming up who deserve their chance," Messi wrote at the time.
Before Tuesday's game, the University of Buenos Aires awarded Messi an honorary doctorate in a ceremony at the Argentine Football Association (AFA) headquarters. Messi, who has in the past spoken of his regret at not studying more, expressed pride at the distinction. "To be able to say that I am an honorary doctor!" he joked.
Outside the Argentina Football Association headquarters, fans unfurled a huge Argentine flag with his image inscribed, "The joy of my life."
Former Barcelona teammate Neymar paid tribute to the departing champion on X. "It's not just Argentina that thanks you, the world thanks you for everything you did for football. Thank you for making me love football even more," he said.
Messi remains under contract with Inter Miami until 2028, although following the death of his father, Jorge, two months ago, he revealed he may hang up his boots for good sooner than anticipated. Messi's departure comes four years after his greatest triumph in international football, leading Argentina to victory at the 2022 World Cup to end the country's 36-year wait for a third title, cementing his status as Diego Maradona's heir.
During his time with the Albiceleste, Argentina won one World Cup, were runners-up twice (Brazil 2014 and North America 2026) and were also crowned Copa America champions in 2021 and 2024.

lemonde.fr/en.title: 'Digger,' by Alejandro González Iñárritu: Tom Cruise as a misanthropic, obscene old man
lemonde.fr/en.text:
LE MONDE'S REVIEW – WORTH SEEING
Brace yourself. Alejandro González Iñárritu, ever the baroque master, takes on the apocalypse in his new film, even if the theme has become almost routine as its imminence grows more apparent by the day. The Mexican director, who has both adapted to and been embraced by Hollywood, last left us in 2022 with mixed feelings after his previous film, Bardo, a somewhat overstuffed autofictional return to his homeland.
Upon reflection, has it ever been otherwise in the cinema of the director of Babel (2006), known for his sprawling ensemble narratives and feats of interwoven editing that stretch across the globe? At least in Birdman (2014) – featuring Michael Keaton as an actor who once basked in the glory of playing a superheroic birdman – he tried to bring a pleasant melancholy to his characteristic gravitas.
This is the spirit in which Digger should be approached, if only Iñarritu's most sardonic comedic frenzy had not taken over. In short, the film falls under the rarely invoked banner of apocalyptic farce, in the vein of Dr. Strangelove (Stanley Kubrick, 1964) or Don't Look Up (Adam McKay, 2021). Here, Digger Rockwell – Tom Cruise transformed into a misanthropic and obscene old man – is a colossal oil tycoon who, fully aware of the consequences, blows up a massive Greenland glacier during drilling operations. The glacier begins drifting toward Europe, threatening to engulf the continent. A crisis unit is formed, led by the president of the United States – John Goodman, noticeably slimmer but in top form – along with other representatives of American military and religious power.

lemonde.fr/en.title: Eva Marie Saint, star of 'North by Northwest' and 'On the Waterfront,' dies at 102
lemonde.fr/en.text:
Eva Marie Saint, the pale, willowy actor who won an Academy Award for her first movie, On the Waterfront, and starred opposite Cary Grant in the Alfred Hitchcock thriller, North by Northwest, has died. She was 102. Saint, whose acting work lasted well into her 90s, died at her home in Los Angeles on Tuesday, October 6, confirmed family representative Jeff Sanderson.
Saint had one of the most spectacular debuts in Hollywood history, as the love interest of Marlon Brando's tormented Terry Malloy in On the Waterfront, and her first trip to the Academy Awards was memorable too. Pregnant with her first child, Saint accepted her Oscar from Frank Sinatra and smilingly murmured a unique winner's speech: "I think I may have the baby right here." Her son, Darrell, was born two days later.
The award for the 1954 classic made her an instant star, but she soon astonished Hollywood with a firm independence that would mark her career. She refused offers of studio contracts and declined chances to follow up on her great success, explaining that she was taking time off to become acquainted with her new son. (A daughter, Laurette, was born in 1958.)
A curated career
In her first decade in Hollywood, Saint appeared in a mere seven films. She declined such top-level productions as The Man in the Gray Flannel Suit with Gregory Peck, Summer and Smoke with Laurence Harvey and The Rainmaker with Burt Lancaster. She credited her husband, TV and stage director Jeffrey Hayden, with persuading her to star in Hitchcock's North by Northwest, the classic 1959 thriller in which Saint plays a spy who seduces Grant, but ends up falling for him.
"I vividly remember him saying, ‘Honey, I think you should find a quiet spot. I'll take care of the children and I want you to really think about this and reread this script,'" she told Vanity Fair in 2014. "He was so right. And that's what husbands are for." Saint was married to Hayden for 55 years, until his death in 2016.
Instead of being put off by her selectivity, studios continued offering her starring roles in such films as Exodus (with Paul Newman), Raintree County (Elizabeth Taylor, Montgomery Clift) and All Fall Down with Warren Beatty.
She turned more to television in the 1970s and enjoyed renewed popularity in the 1980s as the mother of Cybill Shepherd in the hit sitcom, Moonlighting, and as Tom Hanks' mother in the film comedy, Nothing in Common. She won an Emmy for the 1990 miniseries, People Like Us, and had roles in such 21st century movies as Because of Winn-Dixie, Superman Returns and Winter's Tale, adapted from Mark Helprin's novel of the same name. In 2021, she played Marisa Tomei's aunt in the brief audio play, The Bus Ride, part of The Pack Podcast.
Not a stage name
When Saint emerged in the public consciousness, many believed her theatrical-sounding name must have been invented. But she was born with it on July 4, 1924, in Newark, New Jersey. The family moved to Delmar, a small town near Albany, New York, where her father was a Goodrich Rubber Co. manager. Eva's goal was to become a third-grade teacher like her mother, but at Bowling Green State University in Ohio, she tried out for a play and won the leading role.
After graduation, she lived with her parents in Flushing, Long Island, and began hunting for acting jobs in Manhattan. After a fruitless year, she landed a two-line role as a telephone operator on a radio drama and soon was working steadily on soap operas and nighttime dramas, appearing for two years as Claudia on One Man's Family. Network television was booming in the early 1950s, and her looks and dramatic sense made her a favorite with casting people and producers.
Overcoming shyness
A critical turn in Saint's career came when she auditioned before Elia Kazan and was accepted into the Actors Studio, which shaped a generation of method-actor stars. She credited acting coach Lee Strasberg with helping her overcome her shyness. "Lee Strasberg, when he got to know me a little bit, gave me a scene to do where I had to cry in front of my peers," she told the Santa Barbara Independent in 2009. "I worried about it, I worked on it, I tried to use what I was learning at the studio. I finally did the scene, and I cried, and my peers were crying with me. It was just an incredible moment for me."
Saint was rejected for the single female role in the play, Mister Roberts, but was hired to understudy the actor chosen, Jocelyn Brando, Marlon's sister. In six frustrating months, Saint never got to substitute for Brando. She finally made it to Broadway in A Trip to Bountiful, which she had played on television.
Kazan invited her to try out for the female lead in On the Waterfront by improvising a scene with Brando. She was told to try to stop a young man from entering her apartment. She told the Los Angeles Times in 2001: "All I know is that Marlon got in the door and turned on the music. We started dancing. He flicked my skirt. Kazan saw the sparks fly, and that's how I got the part."

lemonde.fr/en.title: French high school protests grow and draw widespread support
lemonde.fr/en.text:
French high school students and their supporters turn out in force for "Act III" of their movement on Tuesday, October 6. The Interior Ministry counted around 266,000 protesters across France, 56,000 in Paris. Meanwhile, high school and university organizers said that 450,000 people joined in the marches, with 100,000 in Paris.
In Lille, Marseille, Lyon, Paris, Clermont-Ferrand and Rennes, high school students who had previously only gathered within the grounds of their schools joined the marches in large numbers. Many were protesting for the first time and the atmosphere was generally good-natured, even though clashes broke out at the end of the Paris protest and the day saw 488 arrests, according to the Interior Ministry.
In Nîmes, among the 13,500 demonstrators counted by the local authorities, four students from Albert-Camus high school also threw their energy into the protest: "There are no incidents in the city today and it's much more pleasant, because maybe we'll finally get heard," said Mathilde, Fantine, Antonin and Melvil. (Le Monde has chosen not to publish the last names of minors.)

lemonde.fr/en.title: Scandals fail to slow Flavio Bolsonaro's political rise in Brazil
lemonde.fr/en.text:
Flavio Bolsonaro never imagined he would find himself so close to the Planalto presidential palace. On Sunday, October 4, after securing 47.03% of the vote in the first round of the presidential election – compared to 45.16% for the incumbent, Lula – the eldest son of the far-right former president (2019-2023), Jair Bolsonaro, seemed surprised by his own result. "I am very satisfied because many polling institutes had predicted we would lose," he told the press, standing with his wife, Fernanda, outside their luxurious home in Brasilia. Under the glare of the cameras, the resemblance to his father was striking: the same thick eyebrows above gray eyes, the same square jaw, the same coarse hair brushed to the side.
When the now 45-year-old senator announced his presidential run in December 2025, the serious corruption allegations that had marked his political career – documented in a 2020 investigation by Rio de Janeiro prosecutors – sparked doubts.
Born on April 30, 1981, from Jair Bolsonaro's first marriage, Flavio was introduced early on by his father both to politics and its illicit practices. In 2002, at the age of 21, he was elected a local MP for Rio de Janeiro, thanks to the support of "Captain" Jair, who taught him the practice of rachadinha: hiring ghost parliamentary aides who kick back between 80% and 90% of their salary to the person who appointed them. "The [Bolsonaro] family fortune was built thanks to the rachadinha," explained Juliana Dal Piva, author of an investigation into the family's assets, O Negócio do Jair ("The Business of Jair," 2022).

lemonde.fr/en.title: Christa Pike is conscious and speaking after botched execution
lemonde.fr/en.text:
The female inmate who survived a failed execution in a US prison last week, Christa Pike, is now conscious and speaking, but her prognosis remains unclear, her lawyers said Tuesday, October 6. Pike, 50, who was sentenced to death for a murder she committed when she was a teenager, received two supposedly lethal doses of the drug pentobarbital at a Tennessee prison a week ago. She survived the injections, however, and was rushed to hospital, where she had been unconscious and on a ventilator in critical condition.
Pike's lawyers said that "against all odds" she was now "conscious, speaking and continues to receive critical medical care." "Despite the severe damage she endured to her arms, she is still handcuffed and shackled to the bed," they said. "Her recovery is medically unprecedented. Her prognosis remains unclear but, at a minimum, we expect a long recovery."
Her lawyers repeated a call for Tennessee Governor Bill Lee to commute Pike's sentence to life imprisonment without the possibility of parole. Lee suspended the carrying out of capital punishment in the southern state following the failed execution pending an independent investigation. The prison chief has resigned.
Pike's case sparked debate over the death penalty for young offenders, as she was 18 when she and her boyfriend beat and killed 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer at a job training camp in 1995. The killing gained national attention after Slemmer's body was found with a pentagram, often seen as a satanic symbol, carved in her chest. Pike's lawyers sought clemency citing her age, childhood sexual abuse and mental health problems, including post-traumatic stress disorder.
According to the Death Penalty Information Center, which publishes data and analysis on capital punishment in the United States, Pike is the first inmate ever to survive "after being injected with lethal doses of execution drugs."

lemonde.fr/en.title: Pneumonic plague: What we know about treatment and transmission of a disease that has 'not disappeared'
lemonde.fr/en.text:
Some diseases are like old ghosts: The mere mention of them can send chills down the spine. The plague is one such disease, bringing with it macabre historical associations, including the death of one in three Europeans during the Black Death in the 14th century. These memories were revived by suspicions arising from Russia after a staff member at the Irkutsk Research Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia died on Friday, October 2.
The Russian authorities' insistence that the situation is under control and that the case is not plague, despite reports in the Russian press over the past four days, has triggered a more recent traumatic memory: the total lack of transparency from China during the early stages of the Covid-19 pandemic.
At this stage, it is difficult to draw any conclusions about the 28-year-old Russian laboratory technician's cause of death. Officially, it was described as "pneumonia of undetermined etiology," according to the governor of the Irkutsk region, Igor Kobzev, who cited analyses carried out by a special expert commission. "No microorganism related to the young woman's professional activities was detected in her biological samples," he stated. In contact with Russia, the World Health Organization (WHO) sought to reassure the public, saying, "The risk to public health for the general population appears to be low."

lemonde.fr/en.title: Ronaldo apologizes to team and supporters for walkout
lemonde.fr/en.text:
Cristiano Ronaldo opened the door for a return to the Portuguese national team on Tuesday, October 6, and apologized for his walkout, while also accusing coach Jorge Jesus of twice breaking his word. "I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team," said Ronaldo in a statement.
Jesus left the forward unused on the bench for a UEFA Nations League match against Norway. Then, before the next game with Denmark said Ronaldo would not start and the 41-year-old walked out. "I owe an apology to my national team teammates for having left the camp," wrote Ronaldo. "Despite the absolute breakdown of trust in the head coach's word... I shouldn't have done it. The responsibility is mine alone."
Ronaldo also apologized to supporters, while explaining his decision. "I apologize to the Portuguese people once again, but a broken word has, for me, a defining impact," said Ronaldo. "I felt that, from that moment on, my presence would only harm the group, and I did what I always said I would do if I didn't feel useful: I picked up my bags and left."
Ronaldo said new Portugal coach Jesus had initially presented him with a plan for the international window which included starting the opening and final games at home, but not traveling for the Nations League matches in Norway and Denmark. The Al-Nassr superstar rejected that proposal, saying it would set a poor example for the captain to remain in Portugal while his teammates traveled.
Ahead of the Norway game, Ronaldo said Jesus unexpectedly asked if he was fit to play 30 minutes. He agreed and warmed up from halftime, without being brought on. "The head coach failed to keep his word to me," said Ronaldo, Portugal's most capped player and all-time top goalscorer.
Former Real Madrid and Manchester United forward Ronaldo said he spoke with Jesus after that and agreed with him that the coach would apologize in a news conference ahead of the Denmark game. However, Ronaldo said Jesus's subsequent press conference was completely different from what was agreed in their conversation, with an "aggressiveness" he had never previously experienced from the coach. "It was the second time he failed to keep his word. I decided to leave the camp without waiting for any further broken promises," wrote Ronaldo.
The striker said he would serve any "suspension that is imposed" on him and accepted he should be punished for his actions."The consequence of this act of mine must be assessed and punished by the Portuguese Football Federation," he explained. "I understand that the punishment should not have mitigating circumstances. I'm not just any player, I'm the team captain, and that is an aggravating factor."
Portugal won all four of their Nations League matches and qualified for the quarter-finals with two games to spare.

lemonde.fr/en.title: Macron makes unexpected appearance at missile test launch from nuclear submarine
lemonde.fr/en.text:
The missile launch was expected, but Emmanuel Macron's presence was not. On Tuesday, October 6, the French president observed, from a frigate positioned off the coast of Brittany, the launch of the latest version of the M51 missile. The weapon is intended for the country's ballistic-missile-capable nuclear submarines (SNLE), which maintain the country's nuclear deterrent at sea. The exercise came at a particularly tense moment, with Russia intensifying its hybrid war against Europe and continuing to brandish the nuclear threat.
The launch, which did not involve a nuclear warhead, was conducted "in strict compliance with France's international commitments," the Armed Forces Ministry emphasized. The missile landed in a predefined area of the Atlantic, several hundred kilometers from the coast. The launch also aimed to demonstrate that Le Vigilant, the SNLE from which the missile was fired, had returned to full operational status after its maintenance and repair period from 2023 to 2025. Such technical overhauls are required for these submarines about every 10 years.

lemonde.fr/en.title: 'The French government's condescension toward high school students shows a refusal to take them seriously as citizens'
lemonde.fr/en.text:
Sociologist Vincent Tiberj is a researcher at the Centre Emile-Durkheim and a professor at Sciences Po Bordeaux. His work focuses on electoral sociology, value systems and, in particular, young people and their relationship with politics. He is notably co-author, with Laurent Lardeux, of Générations Désenchantées? Jeunes et Démocratie ("Disillusioned Generations? Youth and Democracy"), which analyzes young people's political participation and values through statistical surveys. Together with Anja Durovic and Camille Peugny, he coordinates the quantitative study "Demain" ("Tomorrow"), which examines the situation of young people in France in 2026.
How do you interpret the speed and scale of the high school student protests in France?
The way the movement spread gives it an unusually distinctive character. It began in high schools in working-class outskirts of Paris, in Créteil and Saint-Denis, which usually stand on the sidelines of this kind of demonstration, and quickly spread to other high schools with very different social backgrounds and locations. In the Bordeaux area, for example, there were walkouts at high schools both in the generally more privileged city center and in outlying towns such as Dax, La Réole, Libourne and Saintes. The rapid spread of the movement among such diverse groups of young people highlighted their sense of a shared future, with common anxieties and anger.

lemonde.fr/en.title: French policeman charged after firing tear gas grenade at high schooler
lemonde.fr/en.text:
A French policeman was charged Tuesday, October 6, with violence for last week firing a tear gas grenade at close range at a 14-year-old student during high school protests that have shaken the country, a prosecutor said.
The boy, named as Eden, lost most of his teeth and was wounded in the face in the incident in Saint-Ouen-l'Aumone, northwest of Paris, last Monday. The policeman had not been remanded in custody but was placed under judicial control and banned from working until further notice, the local prosecutor said.
In videos of the incident widely shared on social media, three helmeted police officers are seen facing the high school student. One of them strikes the teenager, who kicks him back, before the grenade round fired at his face knocks him to the ground.
Detained for questioning on Monday, the officer said he used the weapon in response to the schoolboy's "resistance," according to the Pontoise prosecutor, Guirec Le Bras, who said "the conditions for self-defense were not been met" due to "the lack of proportionality" in firing the grenade. The offence in question can be punishable by up to 15 years in prison, he said.
The teenager lost several teeth and suffered a fractured jaw that required surgery, the prosecutor's office said. "His jaw is sealed shut, he can no longer speak, and he eats through a straw," his mother told media on Monday, adding all his upper teeth were broken and "his lower teeth torn out."
Police have used tear gas and other means to try to control what the authorities have described as "urban violence" during the protests. Unions, rights groups and many of the children have accused the police of using disproportionate force.

lemonde.fr/en.title: Who is Soumaya Sarré, a student inspiring France's high school protests?
lemonde.fr/en.text:
A popular video creator
"Yo, Macron, you're going too far!" With this slightly informal call-out, Soumaya Sarré, 18, introduces a short, impactful Instagram video. Facing her smartphone, she summed up in late September the frustration felt by some high school students at the start of the school year: "When it comes to telling us how to dress, the State is quick to act, but when it's about ensuring decent learning conditions, suddenly no one's around." In another video, which received more than 45,000 likes, she condemns police violence near a high school. "We're tired of having to wear coats in class because it's so cold," she adds.
A standout student
Since the start of the academic year, Sarré has been pursuing two degrees in history and Arabic language at the Sorbonne in Paris. In July, she graduated with honors from Jean-Renoir high school in the Paris suburb of Bondy, having specialized in history, geopolitics and political science. She feels "comfortable with public speaking," she told Le Monde. On May 13, she won the public speaking competition organized by the Shoah Memorial, which brought together high school students from the three school districts of the Paris region. In her speech, she began by quoting Beate Klarsfeld, who, alongside her husband Serge, tracked down Nazi criminals: "I may not obtain justice, but my quest will not have been in vain."

lemonde.fr/en.title: Hundreds of thousands demonstrate across France for better education
lemonde.fr/en.text:
More than a quarter of a million demonstrators took to the streets across France on Tuesday as unions and teachers joined high school students demanding better learning conditions in protests that later descended into sporadic clashes with security forces. Students have blocked the entrances to hundreds of high schools for 15- to 17-year-olds since late September, complaining of missing teachers, overloaded timetables, dilapidated classrooms and buildings that cannot cope with rising temperatures.
Some 256,000 people took part in student-led protests over calls for better school classroom conditions across France on Tuesday, including 56,000 in the capital Paris, according to the Interior Ministry. Organizers gave a higher figure of 450,000 demonstrators across the country and 100,000 in Paris, as parents, teachers and union workers joined the high school students' movement. At least 488 people were arrested and 43 members of the security forces were wounded on Tuesday, the Interior Ministry announced.
Parents, teachers and union workers joined the high school students' movement in the capital Paris and other cities. At Paris's Place de la République, protesters gathered beneath banners demanding better-funded schools. Two men in climbing gear scaled the nearby monument, where they unfurled a plastic banner reading "Neglected schools, sacrificed youth."
"I'm afraid for my future," Selma, 15, told Agence France-Presse (AFP) without sharing her surname, among the thousands marching in the country's second largest city of Marseille. "We just want to save our education and be educated," said Océane, 18, also at the protest in the southern port city. She said she had suffered from absent teachers who were either not replaced or replaced by "pointless substitutes." "Gen Z has risen up and wants to be heard," 19-year-old Lilia told AFP at a massive march in central Paris, adding she hoped President Emmanuel Macron would listen.
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu condemned violence linked to the protests, telling lawmakers there was "no room for tolerance of violence." "Burning down a high school does not improve the state of high school buildings," he told parliament, rejecting accusations the government had ordered "police repression" against protesters. While many protests have been peaceful, some demonstrators have lit dustbin fires, destroyed bus shelters or clashed with police, who have responded with batons, tear gas grenades and riot-control rounds.
Rights groups, unions and the students have accused authorities of using disproportionate force. A teenager lost a hand on Monday after police fired a stun grenade, while another student reportedly lost several teeth last week after being struck by a police launcher round. The government says 215 students and 715 police officers have been injured since the start of the movement.
A 15-year-old lost a hand to a sting-ball grenade fired by riot officers in the northern town of Lens on Monday. In Metz, prosecutors requested a police inquiry after video footage circulated appearing to show a plainclothes officer inappropriately touching a detained female pupil younger than 15.
Amnesty International late Monday said the French authorities should "put an end to the disproportionate police repression seen in recent days during student protests." "The images and testimonies widely circulated over the past week raise alarming concerns about the dangerous use of tear gas, batons and policing techniques by the police," Amnesty's Anne Savinel-Barras said.
Adults turned out in droves Tuesday to support the young demonstrators. In Rennes, in western France, teacher Romain Dubourg said he and other teachers were present outside the Chateaubriand high school to show support. "With about 30 colleagues, we talked about the police brutality we've witnessed and decided to be there for our students if they need us," he told AFP. The head of the CGT labor union, Sophie Binet, said its members would be there to "protect high-school students."
Since the start of the movement, 24 schools have been burned or ransacked, according to the education ministry. The government is pushing legislation to make those responsible for damaging public property pay for repairs themselves, instead of using public funds.
The unrest has erupted with just months to go before the 2027 election to choose a successor to centrist President Emmanuel Macron, with far-right veteran candidate Marine Le Pen riding high in the polls despite a graft conviction. The government has sought to address the grievances, while accusing the hard-left La France Insoumise(LFI) party of being behind the movement. Veteran LFI presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon has strongly supported the protests, all while calling for non-violent methods.

lemonde.fr/en.title: Three ways Zidane's France is already different from Deschamps'
lemonde.fr/en.text:
Zinédine Zidane made his intentions clear from the outset. On July 28, after signing a four-year contract as head coach of the French national football team, he promised to put his own stamp. "We're going to do things differently," warned the 1998 World Cup winner, making it clear he wanted to break away from the legacy of his predecessor, Didier Deschamps (2012-2026). "DD is DD, Zizou is Zizou," he had said, using their respective nicknames.
The new boss kept his word: During his first two-week camp as France manager, marked by four Nations League matches, he already significantly transformed the face of Les Bleus. Whether in the style of play, his team selection, or his relationship with the media, many major changes were already noticeable.
These new approaches were evident in those four matches: a 1-0 win in Turkey, another victory in Belgium (1-0), a home draw with Italy (1-1) and a final home win against Belgium (4-1).
A revamped formation and philosophy of play
With four attacking players in his starting lineup, Deschamps had chosen a system that favored offense during the World Cup. "Zizou" has opted for a more cautious approach, with three midfielders instead of two, as he did at Real Madrid. He justified the change with his obsession with "balance," aiming to move away from a setup that left the defense exposed during the World Cup semifinal against Spain (0-2).

lemonde.fr/en.title: On Cornell's campus, 'everyone is outraged' by the handling of gang rape case
lemonde.fr/en.text:
A striking procession of several thousand students marched onto Cornell University's main avenue in Ithaca, upstate New York, on Monday, October 5. The protesters gathered beneath the windows of the office of Michael Kotlikoff, the university's president, while loudspeakers were set up and speakers took turns at the microphone, demanding his resignation.
The crowd accused him of covering up reports of gang rape that allegedly took place in a fraternity house, a scandal that has shaken the prestigious university for the past two weeks. The repercussions have been felt across all American campuses, and the controversy has now taken on a political dimension, focusing on how the United States judicial system handles cases of sexual violence.
"Everyone is outraged. It's the only thing anyone can talk about. People are angry and they want concrete change and they're willing to do obviously quite a bit to get it," said Kaori Quan, a doctoral student in history at Cornell, teaching assistant and member of the Graduate Students United union. "It feels fundamentally unsafe to know that I might be teaching in a class, having to have people in my office hours, who are Perpetrators of this kind of crime." Next to her, her friend wore a "Fire Kotlikoff" badge.

welt.de.title: „Wir lagen auf dem Boden und versuchten herauszufinden, wann wir sterben würden“
welt.de.text: Aviva und Keith Siegel waren nach dem 7. Oktober Geiseln der Hamas. Sie erlebten und erlitten auch sexuelle Übergriffe während ihrer Gefangenschaft. Doch die Terrororganisation bestreitet die Gräuel – und viele glauben ihr.

welt.de.title: Pestfall in Russland – Trump bietet Putin Hilfe an
welt.de.text: US-Präsident Donald Trump will nach eigenen Angaben „sehr bald“ mit dem russischen Präsidenten Wladimir Putin über einen möglichen Pestfall in Russland sprechen. Anlass ist der Tod einer Mitarbeiterin des Irkutsker Forschungsinstituts für Seuchenbekämpfung in Sibirien und im Fernen Osten, das unter anderem zur Pest forscht. Die Frau war nach Angaben der russischen Behörden an einer Lungenentzündung unbekannter Ursache gestorben. Auf die Frage nach der Einschätzung der US-Geheimdienste sagte Trump im Weißen Haus, die USA führten dazu „sehr intensive Gespräche“. Voraussichtlich am Mittwoch könne genauer darüber berichtet werden. Trump hatte bereits am Montag erklärt, die USA seien bereit, Russland bei der Bewältigung der Situation zu helfen. „Es ist eine schwere Krankheit“, sagte Trump. Die Weltgesundheitsorganisation (WHO) stufte das Risiko außerhalb Russlands am Dienstag als „sehr gering“ ein. Die UN-Organisation erklärte, sie stehe nach Berichten über den Tod der Institutsmitarbeiterin in Kontakt mit den russischen Behörden. Angespannte Phase zwischen Washington und Moskau Das geplante Gespräch mit Putin fällt in eine angespannte Phase zwischen Washington und Moskau. Die Trump-Regierung muss bis zum 18. Oktober entscheiden, welche russischen Einrichtungen, Unternehmen oder Personen sie nach einem neuen US-Sanktionsgesetz mit Strafmaßnahmen belegen will. Trump hatte den sogenannten Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act am 18. September unterzeichnet. Die Ukraine hat der US-Regierung und dem Kongress eine Liste russischer Unternehmen, Schiffe und Personen vorgelegt, gegen die sie Sanktionen nach dem Gesetz fordert.

welt.de.title: „Das Pendel ist umgeschlagen“ – Israels dramatische Bedrohung von außen und innen
welt.de.text: Vor drei Jahren erschütterte Israel der größte Massenmord seit dem Holocaust. Die Hamas ist immer noch eine Bedrohung, und weltweit erstarkt der Antisemitismus. Aber eine große Gefahr für das Land entsteht auch im Inneren.

welt.de.title: „Tränengas wurde eingesetzt“ – Hunderttausende bei Schülerprotesten in Frankreich
welt.de.text:
In Paris haben sich erneut Zehntausende Menschen zu Protesten versammelt. Neben Schülern beteiligten sich auch Gewerkschaften und Parteien. „Wir haben zum Beispiel etliche Pro-Palästina-Flaggen gesehen“, berichtet Reporter Daniel Kopp.

welt.de.title: Macron will mit Krisensitzung auf Proteste reagieren – Iran bestellt französischen Botschafter ein
welt.de.text: Die Protestwelle junger Menschen in Frankreich für bessere Lernbedingungen an Schulen hat an einem nationalen Aktionstag ein neues Ausmaß erreicht. 256.000 Menschen beteiligten sich nach Angaben des Innenministeriums an Demonstrationen, alleine 56.000 davon in Paris. Die Bildungsgewerkschaften sprachen von 450.000 Demonstranten landesweit. Angesichts der ausufernden Proteste will Präsident Emmanuel Macron nach Medienberichten am Abend auf einer Krisensitzung über die Lage beraten. Daran sollen Premierminister Sébastien Lecornu, Innenminister Laurent Nuñez sowie Bildungsminister Édouard Geffray teilnehmen, berichteten zunächst der Sender BFMTV sowie die Zeitungen „Le Monde“ und „Le Parisien“ unter Verweis auf Informationen aus dem Élysée-Palast. Macron hatte sich bislang nicht in den Umgang mit den Schülerprotesten eingeschaltet, die vor einer Woche begannen. Proteste in zahlreichen Großstädten An zahlreichen Gymnasien und Universitäten kam es an diesem Dienstag zu Blockadeaktionen. In Paris und Großstädten wie Lyon, Lille, Marseille, Toulouse, Bordeaux, Rennes und Straßburg formierten sich Protestzüge, denen sich erstmals auch Gewerkschaften anschlossen. Bei den Protesten für eine bessere Ausstattung der Schulen und bessere Lernbedingungen waren auch Lehrkräfte und Eltern dabei – auch um sich schützend vor ihre Kinder zu stellen. Die Polizei mobilisierte ein Großaufgebot und trat den Demonstranten vielfach in schwerer Montur gegenüber. Sie sieht sich auf den Kundgebungen zunehmend dem Vorwurf von Polizeigewalt ausgesetzt, auf vielen Plakaten prangerten junge Leute den Einsatz von Tränengas an. „Setzt Tränengas gegen Vergewaltiger ein, nicht gegen Minderjährige“, hieß es auf einem Pappschild bei der Kundgebung in Marseille. Auch etliche Politiker empörten sich über das Durchgreifen der Polizei. Die Generalinspektion der Polizei ermittelt wegen Einsätzen, bei denen Demonstranten durch Beamte verletzt wurden. Allerdings wurden auch am Dienstag wieder Beamte mit Gegenständen und Feuerwerkskörpern beworfen, seit Start der Proteste wurden Dutzende Beamte verletzt, alleine am Dienstag 43. Nach Angaben des Innenministeriums gab es am Dienstag 488 Festnahmen. Wie das Justizministerium am Vorabend mitteilte, wurden sei Beginn der Proteste 5060 Menschen festgenommen, 87 Prozent davon Minderjährige. Die bei Ausschreitungen entstandenen Schäden an Schulgebäuden und im öffentlichen Raum bezifferte Justizminister Gérald Darmanin auf mehrere Millionen Euro. Von 1800 frankreichweit blockierten oder vorsorglich geschlossenen Gymnasien sprach die Gymnasialgewerkschaft USL am Dienstag, außerdem seien 90 Prozent der Hochschulen blockiert. Nach Angaben des Bildungsministeriums fiel der Unterricht an 891 Gymnasien ganz oder teilweise aus. Iran beschwert sich Wegen des „gewaltsamen“ Vorgehens französischer Sicherheitskräfte gegen demonstrierende Schüler hat die iranische Regierung unterdessen den französischen Botschafter in Teheran einbestellt. Dem Diplomaten Pierre Cochard sei mitgeteilt worden, dass die französischen Behörden „umfassende und eklatante Menschenrechtsverletzungen“ begangen hätten, berichteten iranische Medien am Dienstag. Im Iran gab es im Winter große regierungskritische Proteste. Die iranischen Behörden erklärten danach, es habe mehr als 3000 Tote gegeben. Sie führten die Gewalt auf von den USA und Israel gesteuerte „Terrorakte“ zurück. Menschenrechtsorganisationen im Ausland sprachen dagegen von einer staatlichen Niederschlagung der Proteste mit tausenden Toten. Bei den vor einer Woche in Schulen im Großraum Paris gestarteten Protesten geht es den Schülern um Probleme, die sie schon seit langem beklagen. Viel zu viel Unterricht falle aus, Vertretungslehrer gebe es zu wenige, etliche Schulgebäude seien heruntergekommen und die Lernbedingungen müssten verbessert werden. Besonders in benachteiligten Stadtteilen fühlen die jungen Leute sich als Menschen zweiter Klasse und mit ihren Sorgen nicht ernst genommen. Premier stellt Verbesserungen an Schulen in Aussicht Zwar rief Premierminister Sébastien Lecornu die Ministerien auf, konkrete Verbesserungen an den Schulen des Landes einzuleiten und den berechtigten Sorgen der Schüler Gehör zu geben. Von Mittwoch bis Freitag sollte an den Schulen über die Probleme diskutiert und nicht unterrichtet werden, sagte Lecornu im Parlament. Und Bildungsminister Geffray schaltete am Montag eine Online-Plattform frei, wo Schüler ihre Forderungen und Probleme schildern können. Damit aber geben sich die jungen Menschen nicht zufrieden. „Wir können diese Repression nicht nachvollziehen. Die überwiegende Mehrheit der Schüler verurteilt Gewalt und Sachbeschädigungen. Wir sind Pazifisten“, sagten die Schülerinnen Iris und Louane einem Reporter der Zeitung „Le Monde“ im westfranzösischen Rennes. „Wir wollen lediglich unseren Forderungen Gehör verschaffen. Das Ausmaß dieser Demonstration wird uns helfen zu zeigen, wie sehr diese Forderungen von vielen geteilt werden.“ Die massiven Proteste treffen Frankreich sieben Monate vor der Präsidentschaftswahl recht unvorbereitet. Die Regierung, die eigentlich gerade mit einem Sparhaushalt ringt, will nun einen Flächenbrand mit einer Ausdehnung der Proteste auf andere Bereiche wie etwa die Hochschulen verhindern. Die Sorge ist, dass die Proteste sich angefacht durch hohe Spritpreise und Lebenshaltungskosten auf andere Bereiche ausweiten könnten und so etwas wie ein zweiter Gelbwestenprotest entsteht, der Frankreich 2019 längere Zeit in Atem hielt.

welt.de.title: „Sollen sie doch Los Angeles auslöschen“ – Trump irritiert mit Aussage
welt.de.text: US-Präsident Donald Trump hat mit Äußerungen zu möglichen Angriffen des Iran auf die US-Metropolen Los Angeles und San Diego für Empörung gesorgt. „Sollen sie doch Los Angeles auslöschen, sollen sie doch San Diego auslöschen“, sagte Trump am Montag bei einer Wahlkampfveranstaltung. Dies sei „ein sehr kleiner Preis“. Die oppositionellen Demokraten, die den Bundesstaat Kalifornien regieren, in dem Los Angeles und San Diego liegen, warfen Trump vor, Teheran zu einem Angriff auf die beiden Städte zu ermutigen. „Donald Trump sagt jetzt, unsere ausländischen Feinde sollten Los Angeles und San Diego ,ausschalten’“, erklärte Kaliforniens Gouverneur Gavin Newsom im Onlinedienst X. „Er ist wirr und gefährlich“, fügte Newsom hinzu. Der Fraktionsvorsitzende der Demokraten im Repräsentantenhaus, Hakeem Jeffries, erklärte auf X: „Die atomare Auslöschung einer US-Stadt ist nicht zum Lachen.“ Videoaufnahmen von Trumps Wahlkampfauftritt im US-Bundesstaat Nebraska waren zuvor viral gegangen. Darin sagte der US-Präsident auch, die hohen Ölpreise durch den Iran-Krieg seien durch die Notwendigkeit gerechtfertigt, Teheran davon abzuhalten, in den Besitz von Atomwaffen zu kommen. Die Ölpreise seien ein „bisschen hoch“, sagte Trump. Dies sei aber „ein kleiner Preis für die Sicherheit der Welt, für die Sicherheit unseres Landes“. Das Weiße Haus wies die Kritik an Trumps Äußerungen am Dienstag als „Medien-Hysterie“ zurück und betonte, der US-Präsident habe über die vom Iran ausgehende Bedrohung gesprochen. „Er stellte eindeutig klar, dass US-Städte bedroht worden wären, wenn ein atomar bewaffneter Iran nicht gestoppt worden wäre“, erklärte Kommunikationschef Steven Cheung auf X. Das Weiße Haus kritisierte auf X zudem eine Schlagzeile der „Los Angeles Times“, wonach Trump vorgeschlagen habe, es solle zugelassen werden, dass der Iran Los Angeles und San Diego „ausschaltet“. „Nein, hat er nicht, ihr Dummköpfe“, erklärte das Weiße Haus dazu. „Er sagte, die USA kämpfen dafür, den Iran daran zu hindern, überhaupt die Fähigkeit zu haben, Los Angeles und San Diego mit einer Atomwaffe auszuschalten – was sie tun würden, wenn sie die Gelegenheit dazu hätten.“ Die USA und Israel hatten ihren am 28. Februar begonnenen Krieg gegen den Iran damit begründet, dass dessen Atomprogramm eine Gefahr darstelle. Die beiden Länder vermuten ebenso wie die Europäer bereits seit Jahrzehnten, dass die Islamische Republik eine Atombombe bauen will, was Teheran kategorisch zurückweist.

welt.de.title: Streit in der EU – Warum Deutschland bei der nächsten großen Erweiterung bremst
welt.de.text: Jetzt ist klar: Die EU ist wild entschlossen, in den kommenden Jahren noch deutlich mehr Länder aufzunehmen – und zwar mindestens acht Staaten. Dabei stehen Montenegro, Albanien, die Ukraine und Moldau ganz vorn auf der Warteliste. Sie dürften die nächsten EU-Mitglieder werden, Montenegro möglicherweise schon 2028,  die Ukraine  (verlinkt auf https://www.welt.de/politik/ausland/article6a2fe0df0611b9299a155e7c/eu-erweiterung-die-eu-oeffnet-der-ukraine-die-naechste-tuer-doch-der-schwierigste-teil-beginnt-erst.html) allerdings erst zu Beginn des neuen Jahrzehnts.  Den neuen EU-Staaten sollen jedoch auch Daumenschrauben angelegt werden. Sie werden laut Plan für viele Jahre deutlich weniger Rechte als die bisherigen 27 Mitgliedsländer haben und können bei Regelverstößen hart sanktioniert werden.  „Unsere Bewertung zeigt, dass die EU noch mehr Länder aufnehmen kann. Aber es gibt da einige Punkte, wo wir Herausforderungen sehen und die wir adressieren müssen“, sagte EU-Erweiterungskommissarin Martha Kos bei der Vorstellung des Berichts mit dem Titel „Vorbereitungen für eine größere Union“ am Dienstag im EU-Parlament in Straßburg.  Wichtig sei, so Kos, dass eine „größere Union auch eine stärkere Union ist“. Die EU-Staats- und Regierungschefs wollen bei ihrem Gipfeltreffen in neun Tagen in Brüssel erstmalig über die Vorschläge beraten.        Dabei sind EU-Länder in der  Erweiterungsfrage (verlinkt auf https://www.welt.de/themen/eu-erweiterung/)  tief gespalten. Es ist damit zu rechnen, dass mehrere der von der EU-Kommission gemachten Vorschläge nicht verabschiedet werden. Wichtige Mitgliedsländer wie Deutschland, Frankreich, Luxemburg, die Niederlande und Belgien fordern besonders hohe Hürden für neue Beitritte und weitreichende sogenannte Schutzklauseln.  Die Regierungen dieser Länder fürchten ansonsten, dass die nationalen Parlamente oder gar die Wähler im Rahmen eines Referendums, wie möglicherweise in Frankreich, gegen eine Erweiterung stimmen könnten.  Ein Kreis weiterer Staaten, der als ‚Freunde des Balkans‘ bekannt ist und von Italien und Österreich angeführt wird, ist jedoch gegen eine sogenannte Zweite-Klasse-Mitgliedschaft der aktuellen Beitrittskandidaten und für zügige Erweiterungsverhandlungen.  „Wer Reformen liefert, muss weiterkommen. Gerade am Westbalkan arbeiten die Menschen seit mehr als 20 Jahren am EU-Beitritt. Die EU muss hier auch Wort halten“, sagte Österreichs Europaministerin Claudia Bauer (ÖVP), die in ihrem Land für Erweiterungsfragen zuständig ist.       Das plant die EU-Kommission konkret:   Erstens:  Es sollen verschiedene Arten von Schutzklauseln („safeguard clauses“) für neue EU-Mitglieder gelten. Bis zu 15 Jahren sollen die Neu-Mitglieder sich schriftlich verpflichten, keine Entscheidungen zu blockieren, die Einstimmigkeit erfordern. Das Veto-Recht soll demnach etwa bei der Verabschiedung von Sanktionen gegen Russland nicht gelten.  Auch sollen die neuen Mitglieder nicht das Recht erhalten, weitere Beitritte zu blockieren. Das ist bedeutend, denn in der Vergangenheit haben EU-Mitglieder versucht, den  Beitritt von Nachbarstaaten zu verhindern (verlinkt auf https://www.welt.de/politik/ausland/article188703171/Skopje-Mazedonien-heisst-nun-offiziell-Nordmazedonien.html) , mit denen es bilaterale Streitigkeiten gab.  Die zweite Schutzklausel, die bereits bestehende Regeln deutlich ausweitet, war intern bis zuletzt umstritten. Sie will die bisherigen EU-Mitglieder gegen eine neue, zu starke wirtschaftliche Konkurrenz und vor Problemen im Justizbereich oder im Agrarsektor schützen.  Die Neu-Mitglieder sollen etwa in einer „Probezeit“, die bis zu zehn Jahre dauern kann, keinen vollen Zugang zum Binnenmarkt oder zur gemeinsamen Agrarpolitik erhalten. Denkbar ist aber auch, dass ihre Rechte in diesen Bereichen bei Verstößen oder schweren Störungen eingeschränkt werden.  Hinzu kommt eine „vorübergehende institutionelle Schutzklausel“. Falls es beispielsweise zu einem „besonders schlimmen Verstoß“ gegen die Werte der EU käme, sollen Stimmrechte vorübergehend aufgehoben werden können, nachdem eine qualifizierte Mehrheit der Mitgliedstaaten dafür gestimmt hat. Diese Regelung soll aber ausschließlich für Neu-Mitglieder gelten.  Damit soll verhindert werden, dass wie in der Vergangenheit ein Land wie  Ungarn weitgehend ungestraft EU-Recht brechen kann (verlinkt auf https://www.welt.de/politik/ausland/article69bc90708f5761671715913a/eu-bricht-mit-ungarn-fast-alle-im-raum-gingen-orban-hart-an.html) . „Wer Rechtsstaatlichkeit aushebelt, muss mit Konsequenzen rechnen. Es geht um den Schutz unserer europäischen Werte und Demokratie, auch innerhalb der Union“, sagte Europaministerin Bauer.       Zweitens:  Beitrittskandidaten sollen nicht mehr wie bisher nach Abschluss der Verhandlungen von heute auf morgen Vollmitglieder der Union werden, sondern der EU schrittweise beitreten („gradual integration“). Der Vorschlag lehnt sich eng an Vorschläge aus Österreich und zuletzt auch von Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz, der eine sogenannte assoziierte Mitgliedschaft vorgeschlagen hatte.  Demnach sollen die Beitrittskandidaten je nach Fortschritt den verschiedenen Sektoren der EU, wie teilweise der Verkehrs- und Umweltpolitik oder dem Binnenmarkt, schrittweise beitreten können. Jährliche Dialoge zwischen EU und den Kandidaten sollen die Fortschritte bewerten.  EU-Roaming bereits für Ukraine und Moldau Ansatzweise gibt es eine solche schrittweise Integration bereits. So gelten die europäischen Roaming-Regeln schon heute auch für die Ukraine und Moldau, und diverse Beitrittsländer beteiligen sich an dem einheitlichen europäischen Zahlungsverkehr (SEPA).       Drittens:  Die EU-Kommission soll nach einer Erweiterung verkleinert werden. Das hat bereits der EU-Vertrag von Lissabon aus dem Jahr 2009 vorgesehen. Passiert ist seitdem nichts. Künftig sollen nur zwei Drittel der Mitgliedstaaten einen Kommissar stellen dürfen. Es soll nach dem Rotationsprinzip verfahren werden, damit kein Land zu kurz kommt.  Der Plan dürfte vor allem bei kleineren Mitgliedstaaten auf Ablehnung stoßen, denn für sie ist der nationale EU-Kommissar häufig der einzige Anlaufpunkt in Brüssel und darum besonders wichtig. Österreichs Europaministerin Bauer sagte: „Eine größere EU braucht eine kleinere EU-Kommission. Wir brauchen schlankere Strukturen und schneller Entscheidungen. Sparen im System muss auch in Brüssel gelten.“    Viertens:  Die EU-Kommission schlägt vor, bereits vorhandene Instrumente zu nutzen, um Entscheidungen zu beschleunigen. So erlaubt es die sogenannte Brückenklausel („passarelle“), dass die Mitgliedstaaten außer im Verteidigungsbereich Entscheidungen, die bisher einen einstimmigen Beschluss erfordern, auf eine qualifizierte Mehrheit umzustellen, sodass Blockaden erschwert werden und zügiger entschieden wird. Der Beschluss erfordert aber Einstimmigkeit und ist darum noch niemals angewendet worden. Es ist und bleibt wohl ein frommer Wunsch.  Die Kommissionsbehörde befürwortet auch, das Instrument der sogenannten verstärkten Zusammenarbeit („enhanced cooperation“) künftig stärker zu nutzen. Es ermöglicht einem Kreis von mindestens neun Mitgliedstaaten, die Zusammenarbeit zu vertiefen und weitere Integrationsschritte zu gehen. In fünf Fällen ist das bisher gelungen, etwa beim Ehescheidungsrecht oder beim Patentschutz. Es könnte viel mehr passieren, aber die Mitgliedstaaten sperren sich dagegen. Das dürfte auch so bleiben.       Fünftens:  Eine Sonderregel für die Ukraine. Wegen der Größe und Leistungsfähigkeit der ukrainischen Landwirtschaft sollen bestimmte landwirtschaftliche Produkte nur einen begrenzten Zugang zum EU-Markt haben. Gleichzeitig will Brüssel die Ukraine dabei unterstützen, mehr Agrarprodukte nach Afrika oder Asien zu verkaufen. Ohne diese Ausnahmeregelung hätten etwa deutsche und  polnische Bauern (verlinkt auf https://www.welt.de/politik/ausland/article250277456/Bauernproteste-160-Tonnen-Getreide-in-Polen-zerstoert-Ukraine-fordert-Bestrafung.html)  massiv gegen die mächtige Konkurrenz aus der Ukraine protestiert.       Erweiterung bleibt ein Zankapfel Der Plan von Erweiterungskommissarin Kos ist der ehrenwerte Versuch, die Kritiker von weiteren EU-Beitritten zu besänftigen. Das dürfte mehrere Beitrittskandidaten verärgern. Gleichzeitig könnte es nicht ausreichen, um die Skeptiker in vielen Mitgliedstaaten wie Frankreich ruhigzustellen.  Die Erweiterung, die lange als Erfolgsmodell der EU galt, weil so Stabilität nach außen exportiert wurde, ist ein Zankapfel – und wird es auch bleiben. Die Sorgen vieler Bürger in den 27 Mitgliedsländern vor Kriminalitätsimport und immensen Kosten für die Steuerzahler bleiben weiterhin bestehen. Martha Kos’ Pläne ändern daran nichts.  Christoph B. Schiltz  (verlinkt auf https://www.welt.de/autor/christoph-schiltz/) ist Korrespondent in Brüssel. Er berichtet unter anderem über Sicherheits- und Verteidigungspolitik der EU, die europäische Migrationspolitik, die Nato und Österreich.

welt.de.title: Großoffensive „Morgenröte“ – Wie mächtige Akteure die Macht der Huthi brechen wollen
welt.de.text: Der Vormarsch der Huthi-Miliz im Jemen schien ungebrochen. Nun melden Regierungstruppen Geländegewinne rund um die wichtige Meerenge Bab al-Mandab. Mächtige Akteure wittern eine günstige Gelegenheit.

welt.de.title: „Propagandisten machen sich lustig über das, was vom BND-Chef gesagt wurde“
welt.de.text:
BND-Präsident Martin Jäger hat vor einem immer aggressiveren Auftreten Russlands und einem gewaltsamen Konflikt mit dem Land gewarnt. „Wir kennen die Provokationen aus Russland schon lange“, so Axel Springer Global Reporter Paul Ronzheimer
